gp.text: Gross margin was $308.6 million in 2025, representing a 5% decrease from $326.0 million in 2024. Gross margin expressed as a percentage of net sales was 17% in 2025 and 19% in 2024. Gross margin expressed as a percentage of value-added sales was 29% in 2025 and 30% in 2024. Gross margin decreased from the prior year primarily related to lower sales volumes and $25.7 million of charges in the Performance Materials segment related to the quality issue described above. Gross margin in 2024 was unfavorably impacted by higher costs associated with the production ramp of the precision clad strip facility.

oi.text: Other non-operating income-net includes components of pension and post-retirement income other than service costs. Refer to Note P of the Consolidated Financial Statements for details of the components of net periodic benefit costs.

nonop.text: Interest expense - net was $30.7 million in 2025 and $34.8 million in 2024. The decrease in interest expense in 2025 compared to 2024 is primarily due to a decrease in interest rates and borrowings compared to the prior year.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $103.2 million in 2025 versus $87.8 million in 2024. The increase of $15.4 million was primarily driven by a $33.5 million increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses, compared to a $15.8 million decrease in the prior year, resulting in a favorable cash inflow impact of $49.3 million. This improvement was mainly due to the timing of year-end payments and ongoing working capital management initiatives. This increase was partially offset by higher inventory levels, which increased by $13.3 million compared to the prior year, reflecting operational and quality challenges experienced in the fourth quarter of 2025. Additionally, accounts receivable increased by $22.1 million relative to the prior year, driven by timing differences in collections and reduced accounts receivable factoring in the current year.

wc.text: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $103.2 million in 2025 versus $87.8 million in 2024. The increase of $15.4 million was primarily driven by a $33.5 million increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses, compared to a $15.8 million decrease in the prior year, resulting in a favorable cash inflow impact of $49.3 million. This improvement was mainly due to the timing of year-end payments and ongoing working capital management initiatives. This increase was partially offset by higher inventory levels, which increased by $13.3 million compared to the prior year, reflecting operational and quality challenges experienced in the fourth quarter of 2025. Additionally, accounts receivable increased by $22.1 million relative to the prior year, driven by timing differences in collections and reduced accounts receivable factoring in the current year.

capex.text: We believe that cash flow from operations plus available borrowing capacity and our current cash balance are adequate to support operating requirements, capital expenditures, projected pension plan contributions, the current dividend and selective share repurchases, environmental remediation projects, and strategic acquisitions for at least the next 12 months and the foreseeable future thereafter. At December 31, 2025, cash and cash equivalents held by our foreign operations totaled $13.0 million. We do not expect restrictions on repatriation of cash held outside of the United States to have a material effect on our overall liquidity, financial condition, or the results of operations for the foreseeable future.

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text: Net sales consist primarily of revenue from the sale of precious and non-precious specialty metals, beryllium and copper-based alloys, beryllium composites, and other products into numerous end markets. The Company requires an agreement with a customer that creates enforceable rights and performance obligations. We recognize revenue, in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the Company expects to be entitled, when we satisfy a performance obligation by transferring control of a product to the customer. The core principle of the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 606 is supported by five steps which are outlined below with management's judgment in applying each.

Semiconductor.text: At the Company level, volume increased in the semiconductor (21%), telecom and data center (24%) and energy (12%) end markets. Additionally, sales of raw material beryllium hydroxide increased by $6.3 million compared to the prior year. The increase was partially offset by a volume decrease in the consumer electronics (30%) end market due to a quality issue with a large precision clad strip customer within Performance Materials segment, causing the Company to temporarily idle production facilities, which limited sales in the fourth quarter. The Company closely collaborated with our customer, implementing targeted modifications to our processes and procedures and enhancing quality control measures designed to reduce the risk of future occurrences. We resumed shipping product from our facilities in December 2025 and continue to ramp production.

Energy.text: At the Company level, volume increased in the semiconductor (21%), telecom and data center (24%) and energy (12%) end markets. Additionally, sales of raw material beryllium hydroxide increased by $6.3 million compared to the prior year. The increase was partially offset by a volume decrease in the consumer electronics (30%) end market due to a quality issue with a large precision clad strip customer within Performance Materials segment, causing the Company to temporarily idle production facilities, which limited sales in the fourth quarter. The Company closely collaborated with our customer, implementing targeted modifications to our processes and procedures and enhancing quality control measures designed to reduce the risk of future occurrences. We resumed shipping product from our facilities in December 2025 and continue to ramp production.

Other.heading: Other considerations
Other.text:
We receive payment from customers equal to the invoice price for most of our sales transactions.

Returned products are generally not accepted unless the customer notifies the Company in writing, and we authorize the product return by the customer.

Unearned revenue is recorded cash consideration from customers in advance of the shipment of the goods, which is a liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. This contract liability is subsequently reversed and the revenue, cost of sales, and gross margin are recorded when the Company has transferred control of the product to the customer. The related inventory also remains on our balance sheet until the revenue recognition criteria are met. Advanced billings are typically made in association with products with long manufacturing times and/or products relating to contracts with the government. Billings in advance of the shipments allow us to collect cash earlier than billing at the time of the shipment and, therefore, the collected cash can be used to reduce our investment in working capital. Refer to Note D of the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional details on our contract balances.

gp.text: Gross margin in the third quarter of 2026 was $103.7 million, an increase of 20% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Gross margin expressed as a percentage of net sales was 18% and 19% in the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Gross margin expressed as a percentage of value-added sales was 33% in both the third quarter of 2026 and 2025. Gross margin as a percentage of value-added sales remained flat in both the third quarter of 2026 and 2025.

nonop.text: Interest expense-net was $6.6 million and $7.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in interest expense is primarily due to a decrease in interest rates and borrowings compared to the prior-year period.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $142.7 million in the first nine months of 2026 versus $83.7 million in the prior-year period. In addition to the $31.3 million increase in operating income, the increase in cash provided by operating activities was favorably impacted by the Company’s continued working capital initiatives, specifically efforts focused around timing of quarter-end payments related to payables and accruals. This resulted in incremental cash flow of $38.4 million, when comparing to the first nine months of 2025. Additionally, prepaids and other current assets decreased $0.4 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared to an increase of $21.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, generating $19.8 million in operating cash flow. This was primarily due to a $3.3 million decrease in unbilled receivables in the first nine months of 2026, compared to a $14.9 million increase in the prior-year period. These cash inflows were partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable of $46.7 million to support sales growth in the first nine months of 2026, compared to a decrease of $1.7 million in the first nine months of 2025, resulting in a cash outflow of $48.5 million.

intro.text: Materion Corporation (referred to herein as the Company, our, we, or us), through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is an integrated producer of high-performance advanced engineered materials used in a variety of electrical, electronic, thermal, and structural applications with $1.8 billion in net sales in 2025. The Company was incorporated in Ohio in 1931. Our products are sold into numerous end markets, including semiconductor, industrial, aerospace and defense, automotive, energy, consumer electronics, and life sciences. Our businesses are organized under four reportable segments: Performance Materials, Electronic Materials, Precision Optics, and Other. Our Other reportable segment includes unallocated corporate costs. Additional information regarding our segments and business is presented below.

Gross margin decreased from the prior year primarily due to impact of lower volumes and related unabsorbed costs in the first half of 2024. Additionally, gross margin was unfavorably impacted by higher costs associated with the production ramp of the precision clad strip facility.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $87.8 million in 2024 versus $144.4 million in 2023. The decrease in net cash provided by operating activities was primarily driven by working capital outflows in 2024 compared to 2023. Continued focus on working capital resulted in flat inventory and relatively flat accounts receivable balances as of December 31, 2024 compared to the December 31, 2023, as opposed to a net cash inflow in 2023 of $4.7 million in the prior year when these efforts began. Additionally, in line with the Company's cost savings initiatives, accounts payable and accruals decreased in 2024 compared to an increase in accounts payable in 2023, creating an unfavorable impact to operating cash flows of $22.4 million. In addition, there was a $16.7 million decrease in operating cash flow due to lower unearned income for customer prepayments related to the agreements with a customer as discussed in Note K. Lastly , the decrease in unearned revenue due to an increase in shipments for customers which prepaid had an unfavorable impact to operating cash flow $7.3 million when compared to the prior year.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Prior to this, no single customer accounted for ten percent or more of our net sales.
In 2025, 20% of our value-added sales were to customers in the aerospace and defense end market.
In fiscal year 2025, no customers accounted for more than ten percent of our sales.
Revenue from international operations (principally Europe and Asia) accounted for approximately 64% in 2025, 57% in 2024 and 51% in 2023, respectively of Net sales.
In fiscal 2025, no customers accounted for more than 10 percent of our net sales.

The impact of this potential adverse effect would depend on the nature and extent of the changes to the standards, the cost and ability to meet the new standards, the extent of any reduction in customer use, and other factors.
For instance, our manufacturing facility in Elmore, Ohio relies on our mining operation for its supply of beryllium hydroxide used in production of most of its beryllium-containing materials.
In addition, many of our manufacturing facilities depend on one source for electric power and natural gas, which could be interrupted due to equipment failures, terrorism, or another cause.
The timing of the share repurchases will depend on several factors, including market and business conditions, our cash flow, debt levels, and other investment opportunities.
We rely on estimates of our ore resources and recoverable reserves, which estimation is complex due to geological characteristics of the properties and the number of assumptions made.
